import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_46/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_46/training_1.csv"

Source3_46_0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
Source3_46_1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_46_0 and Source3_46_1 on "city"
# According to the operation history, join on city column
joined_df = pd.merge(Source3_46_0, Source3_46_1, on="city", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by = [Source3_46_0.city, Source3_46_0.type]
# aggregations = [sum(Source3_46_0.driver_count), avg(Source3_46_1.fare), count(Source3_46_1.ride_id)]

# Group by city and type (from Source3_46_0)
grouped = joined_df.groupby(['city', 'type'], as_index=False).agg(
    driver_count=('driver_count', 'sum'),
    Average_Fare=('fare', 'mean'),
    Ride_Count=('ride_id', 'count')
)

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
# Target schema: ['city': string, 'driver_count': integer, 'type': string, 'Average Fare': float, 'Ride Count': integer]
# Note: 'Average Fare' and 'Ride Count' have spaces, so rename accordingly
grouped.rename(columns={
    'Average_Fare': 'Average Fare',
    'Ride_Count': 'Ride Count'
}, inplace=True)

# Ensure data types match target schema
grouped['city'] = grouped['city'].astype(str)
grouped['driver_count'] = grouped['driver_count'].astype(int)
grouped['type'] = grouped['type'].astype(str)
grouped['Average Fare'] = grouped['Average Fare'].astype(float)
grouped['Ride Count'] = grouped['Ride Count'].astype(int)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_46/target_multisource.csv"
grouped.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 as per hint 21
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_46/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_46/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city (inner join to keep only matching cities)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', on='city')

# Group by city, driver_count, type (leftmost non-float unique columns in target)
# Aggregate avg fare and count ride_id
result = joined.groupby(['city', 'driver_count', 'type'], as_index=False).agg(
    **{
        'Average Fare': ('fare', 'mean'),
        'Ride Count': ('ride_id', 'count')
    }
)

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_46/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
